punchline: A meeting where nobody disagrees may just be moving its arguments to the hallway afterward.
thirty_sec: Lencioni calls the quiet, agreeable meeting artificial harmony. Everyone nods, the agenda finishes on time, and the real opinions come out afterward in back-channel comments. He says the fix is conflict about ideas, not people, and that a leader should mine for it: pull the buried disagreement into the room and resist rescuing everyone from the discomfort. Teams that argue openly, he says, settle issues faster because nothing is left to be said in a side conversation later.
